claims.text: The terbium-free refractory high-entropy alloy is non-superconducting in the low-temperature regime.
Terbium incorporation alters the alloy's electronic structure.
Terbium incorporation alters the local lattice environment.
The terbium-induced changes enhance electron-phonon coupling.
Terbium may introduce magnetic fluctuations that are beneficial for superconducting pairing.
Terbium addition enables low-temperature superconductivity that is absent from the terbium-free alloy.
Terbium incorporation modifies the crystal structure.
Terbium incorporation modifies the local electron-density distribution.
Terbium may introduce localized magnetic moments that affect the band structure near the Fermi level.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling and terbium-associated magnetic fluctuations facilitate unconventional pairing.
The proposed electronic and magnetic effects lower the free-energy barrier for superconductivity.
The terbium-alloyed sample will exhibit a finite superconducting critical temperature.
The terbium-free control will remain in the normal state under identical low-temperature conditions.
Terbium concentrations below a moderate doping regime may be insufficient to alter the electronic environment enough to induce superconductivity.
Excessive terbium may suppress superconductivity through magnetic pair breaking.
Magnetic impurities can enhance unconventional pairing in some regimes and act as pair breakers in others.
The doped and undoped samples are to receive identical arc-melting, homogenization, annealing, and measurement conditions.
Zero electrical resistance together with a Meissner response is the designated evidence for a superconducting transition.

contradictions.description: The query describes the selected alloy's superconducting behavior as uncharacterized, whereas the initial-state and baseline fields assert that the terbium-free alloy is already known to be non-superconducting in the test regime.
